name: Bane
label: Equal Vision Records
lede: A Converge guitarist's side project from Worcester turned into two decades of stage dives, one record kids still tattoo on themselves, and a goodbye tour that took two years to finish.

eras.title: A Converge side project in Worcester
eras.text: Aaron Dalbec was playing guitar in Converge when he and Damon Bellorado started a band on the side in central Massachusetts. Aaron Bedard took over the microphone, and Bane spent its first years playing every hall and basement between Worcester and Boston.

years.h: Aaron Dalbec and Damon Bellorado start Gateway in Worcester
years.p: Converge guitarist Aaron Dalbec and Damon Bellorado start a side project in Worcester, Massachusetts. It is called Gateway before it becomes Bane.

years.h: Gateway becomes Bane, and Aaron Bedard takes the mic
years.p: The band renames itself Bane. First singer Matt Firestone doesn't last; Aaron Bedard takes over vocals and Zach Jordan joins on guitar, the core that would still be there two decades later.

years.h: Bane record their first five-song demo
years.p: In December 1995 Bane cut a five-song demo tape, the start of a run of small-label releases around central Massachusetts.

years.h: Both Guns Blazing lands on They Came From Massachusetts
years.p: Bane's song Both Guns Blazing appears on Big Wheel Recreation's 1996 compilation of Massachusetts hardcore bands.

years.h: Forked Tongue EP on Life Records
years.p: Bane's first proper release comes out on Life Records in May 1996.

years.h: Free to Think, Free to Be, Bane's second Life EP
years.p: A second EP for Life Records. Damon Bellorado leaves in 1997, and Ben Chused plays drums for about a year.

eras.title: Equal Vision and the long drive
eras.text: Equal Vision Records gathered Bane's early songs onto one release and put the band in a van for its first national tours. Two albums later, with Brian McTernan behind the board, Bane had made the record a generation of hardcore kids would measure everything against.

years.h: Holding This Moment: Bane's first Equal Vision release
years.p: Equal Vision collects Bane's earlier material as a 7" and CD. The same year the band heads out on its first US tour, with Nick Branigan now on drums.

years.h: It All Comes Down to This, cut in Clinton, Massachusetts
years.p: Bane's first full-length is recorded in June 1999 at Austin Enterprises in Clinton, Massachusetts, and released by Equal Vision.

years.h: Bane tour North America with Death by Stereo and Adamantium
years.p: A North American run with [[Death by Stereo|62c2f99c-d777-4ca5-8602-548807cfb824]] and Adamantium, plus Bane's first shows in Europe. They also cover [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]]'s Just How Much for a compilation.

years.h: Kurt Ballou records the Bane/Adamantium split
years.p: In early September 2000 Converge's [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] produces Bane's side of a split 7" with Adamantium. Indecision Records releases it in 2001.

years.h: Give Blood comes out on Halloween 2001
years.p: Recorded that August with Brian McTernan in Beltsville, Maryland: Bedard, Dalbec, Jordan, Pete Chilton on bass and Nick Branigan on drums. About 25 minutes about the hardcore scene, dreams and loss.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes Give Blood as focused on the hardcore scene itself, with themes of dreams and loss. Lambgoat gave it 9 out of 10.

Bane had claimed straight edge on an early release, but it was never their main subject. The band's original members stayed straight edge; later drummer Bob Mahoney and bassist Stu Maguire did not.

eras.title: The Note, and a new drummer
eras.text: Bob Mahoney took over the drums and Bane went further than a Worcester band had any right to, from Japan to Europe. The Note was their second album with McTernan, and the last with bassist Pete Chilton.

years.h: Bob Mahoney replaces Nick Branigan on drums
years.p: Nick Branigan leaves after five years and Bob Mahoney takes the drum stool. He stays until the end, and comes back for every reunion.

years.h: Bane spend two weeks touring Japan
years.p: In April 2004 Bane play a two-week tour of Japan, one of the band's first long runs overseas.

years.h: Bane tour the US with Comeback Kid and With Honor
years.p: A March 2005 US run with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]] and With Honor, two bands that grew up on Bane records.

years.h: The Note, recorded at Salad Days Studios
years.p: Bane's third album, again with Brian McTernan, this time at his Salad Days Studios. Equal Vision releases it in 2005.

years.h: Ten Years Plus E.P. marks a decade of Bane
years.p: Equal Vision issues the Ten Years Plus E.P. for the band's tenth anniversary.

years.h: Bane cover We Stand Alone; Pete Chilton leaves
years.p: Bane record [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]]'s We Stand Alone for the tribute Our Impact Will Be Felt. Bassist Pete Chilton, there since the start, leaves the band.

eras.title: Live from everywhere
eras.text: With Stu Maguire on bass, Bane toured the world and put out three live albums named for cities and clock times. Then, as the band neared twenty years, they started work on a record they announced would be their last.

years.h: Brendan "Stu" Maguire joins on bass
years.p: Stu Maguire, known from Boston's Reach the Sky, takes over bass. He had also worked for the [[Dropkick Murphys|e8374874-4178-4869-b92e-fef6bf30dc04]] and [[The Mighty Mighty Bosstones|779353f3-6401-4cda-a8a2-6fd3ec9bc11b]].

years.h: Three live albums, each named for a city and a time
years.p: Tokyo 7:58am (Alliance), Boston 6:58pm (Triple-B) and Los Angeles 3:58pm (6131) all come out in 2009. Overseas they become Perth, Curitiba, Dublin and Rome.

years.h: Stu Maguire leaves; Chris Linkovich takes the bass
years.p: Stu Maguire's run ends and Chris Linkovich plays bass through 2014. Bane also cut Satan's Son for Triple-B's America's Hardcore Volume 2.

years.h: Bane start recording their final album
years.p: Alternative Press reports in December 2013 that Bane have begun recording what they say will be their last album.

eras.title: The two-year goodbye
eras.text: Bane announced the end and then took their time: a final album, a world tour, and a last run of hometown shows. Few hardcore bands have ever planned their own funeral this carefully.

years.h: Don't Wait Up, Bane's announced final album
years.p: Alternative Press premieres Don't Wait Up in May 2014. Bane call it their last record but say they will keep touring. James Siboni joins on bass.

years.h: Bane's last New York show, at Webster Hall
years.p: On the farewell tour, Bane play Webster Hall in New York City on May 8, 2016. IDIOTEQ later called it their final concert.

years.h: Bane's final show, at the Worcester Palladium
years.p: Bane end where they started: the Worcester Palladium on June 18, 2016. [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]] and The Promise are on the bill, per Lambgoat.
years.xp: The farewell stretched across two years and several continents after Don't Wait Up. Wikipedia dates the very last show to June 18, 2016, at the Palladium in Worcester, twenty-odd years after Gateway started a few miles away.

eras.title: For Stu, and then for good
eras.text: Bane stayed retired until the death of their former bassist brought them back for one night. Two years later they admitted they missed it and booked Boston.

years.h: Stu Maguire is diagnosed with pancreatic cancer
years.p: Former Bane bassist Stu Maguire, in his early 40s, is diagnosed with pancreatic cancer after six months of seeking answers. His family sells merch to cover treatment, and Bane ask fans to help.

years.h: Stu Maguire dies of pancreatic cancer
years.p: Brendan "Stu" Maguire, Bane's bassist from 2008 to 2012, dies on June 27, 2021, of pancreatic cancer.

years.h: Bane reunite by surprise at Stu Maguire's benefit
years.p: Five days after Stu Maguire's death, Bane turn up unannounced at a benefit in his honor with [[The Bouncing Souls|429d5f26-329c-41cc-bdff-17c29dbf1fb8]], [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]], [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]] and Rebuilder.

q: We missed this too much. We missed you too much.
years.h: Bane announce a reunion at Roadrunner in Boston
years.p: In the early hours of February 7, 2023, Bane announce a return at Roadrunner in Boston on June 17, with [[The Suicide File|86336490-e9fb-41e3-9a81-8edfa56785ec]], [[Stick to Your Guns|07ef6bdd-20c8-4f2b-ac87-463f65b90768]] and [[Modern Life Is War|1bfdbf9d-e241-4ad7-8283-a3a7904bb6ca]].
years.xp:
IDIOTEQ called it a one-time performance; Wikipedia describes it as a two-night event at Roadrunner. Either way, Bane insisted on an all-ages show with no barricade between band and crowd.

Bracewar and Colin of Arabia filled out the bill.
